u0: The agent has no outstanding obligations: no client is waiting to have an order taken or served, and no portion of food has just slipped and needs to be regained on the next step. The agent is up to date and can wait for the next client to arrive. A new client arrival will create an order-taking commitment, taking an order will create a serving commitment, and a fresh food slip will create an immediate recovery commitment.
u1: A client's order has been taken, and that order is still waiting to be served. No client is currently waiting to have an order taken, and no fallen food needs immediate recovery. The remaining objective is to serve the taken order; if food slips before then, recovering it on the very next step becomes an additional urgent obligation. Serving the client clears the outstanding client commitment.
u2: Food has just slipped out of the agent's hands, and the agent must be holding food again on the very next step. No client order is outstanding: no one is waiting to have an order taken, and no taken order remains unserved. Regaining the food immediately clears the outstanding commitment; failing to hold food on the next step is a permanent failure.
u3: An order has already been taken and is still awaiting service, and food has just slipped so it must be back in the agent's hands on the very next step. The food recovery is urgent: if the agent is not holding food on the next step, the task fails for good. Once the food is recovered, the taken order remains and must still be served.
u4: A client is waiting at the counter and their order has not yet been taken. No taken order is awaiting service and no fallen food needs immediate recovery. The immediate client objective is to take that order; after it is taken, serving it becomes the remaining obligation. If food slips before the order is taken, regaining it on the next step becomes an additional urgent commitment.
u5: A client is waiting whose order has not yet been taken, and food has just slipped so it must be back in the agent's hands on the very next step. The food recovery must not be missed, or the task fails permanently. If the food is recovered, the client's order still needs to be taken and then served.
u6: Both kinds of client commitment are outstanding at once: a client still needs to have an order taken, and an order that was already taken still needs to be served. No fallen food requires immediate recovery. The agent must resolve both obligations; taking an order would clear the untaken-order obligation while leaving the unserved-order obligation, and serving would clear the unserved-order obligation while leaving the untaken-order obligation.
u7: Three commitments are pending together: an order is waiting to be taken, an earlier taken order is still waiting to be served, and food has just slipped so it must be held again on the very next step. The food recovery is urgent, and missing it fails the task permanently. If the food is recovered, both client obligations remain until the waiting order is taken and the earlier order is served.
u8: A mandatory requirement has been violated: food slipped from the agent's hands and was not being held again on the very next step. That immediate-recovery rule is broken beyond repair, so successful completion of the task is no longer possible. Any other client obligations cannot make up for this failure.
